concepts.title: Natural Resources
concepts.definition: Natural resources are the gifts of nature that humans use to live and prosper - air, water, soil, forests, grasslands, fish, minerals and energy sources - taken straight from the environment rather than manufactured by people.
concepts.key_idea: Anything useful drawn directly from nature counts as a natural resource.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees101.txt lines 1-90 (natural resources and their categories)
question_patterns: what are natural resources - define with examples
name five natural resources used in daily life

why are air and water called natural resources

solution_steps.explain: The material must come directly from nature, not from a factory.
It must satisfy human needs such as food, energy or materials.
Place it among air, water, soil, forest, mineral or energy resources.

concepts.title: Renewable and Non-Renewable Resources
concepts.definition: Resources split by their ability to return: renewable resources like sunlight, wind, water and forests can regenerate within a human timescale if used carefully, while non-renewable resources like coal, petroleum and minerals take millions of years to form, so their stock only shrinks with use.
concepts.key_idea: Sunlight returns tomorrow; coal burned today is gone for good.
question_patterns: differentiate renewable and non-renewable resources with examples
why is coal called a non-renewable resource
is groundwater always renewable - explain
classify sunlight, petroleum, wind and iron ore as renewable or not
what happens if renewable resources are used faster than they regrow
which category of resources should be conserved most strictly and why

solution_steps.explain: Check whether the resource refills itself in a useful span of time.
Flowing and growing resources are renewable; fossil stocks and minerals are not.
Renewables need careful use, non-renewables need saving and substitution.

concepts.title: Distribution of Natural Resources
concepts.definition: Nature has not shared its riches evenly: oil pools under West Asia, minerals lie in particular belts and rivers drain specific highlands, so different regions of India and the world hold different resources, shaping trade, settlements and even disputes like the sharing of Kaveri waters.
concepts.key_idea: Where a resource sits decides where industry grows and how regions trade.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees101.txt lines 295-460 (distribution of natural resources, Kaveri dispute)
question_patterns: why are natural resources unevenly distributed across the world
how does the distribution of resources affect trade between regions
name a resource rich region of India and its resources
how can river water become a source of dispute between states
why do industries grow near mineral belts
explain how uneven distribution shapes human settlements

solution_steps.explain: Note where geology and climate place each resource.
Settlements, farms and industries cluster where resources allow.
Trade networks and sharing disputes follow from unequal distribution.

concepts.title: Responsible and Wise Use of Resources
concepts.definition: Because resources are finite or slow to renew, wise use means the three R's - reduce what we consume, reuse what we can, recycle materials - along with conserving water and soil and shifting to renewable energy so future generations inherit working resources.
concepts.key_idea: Reduce, reuse, recycle - sustainable habits keep resources alive for tomorrow.
question_patterns: what is meant by sustainable use of natural resources
explain the three R's with one example each
how can a household conserve water and electricity
why must resources be saved for future generations
how does recycling paper help forests
suggest a resource conservation plan for your school

solution_steps.explain: Using less and reusing items lowers the pressure on nature.
Recycling turns waste into raw material again.
Renewable energy and careful water use stretch the resource base.
